parsed.notes: Lens B reviewed only currency, treatment, existence, and authority-weight issues. No support or quote-fidelity defect is raised.

reasons: Lake identity record is verified for Cady v. Dombrowski, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1973-06-21.
Lake citations include official citation 413 U.S. 433, parallel cites 93 S. Ct. 2523 and 37 L. Ed. 2d 706, and vendor-neutral cite 1973 U.S. LEXIS 48.
Top-level lake treatment marks field_i_validity as good_law, so the disclosed record does not show the authority is dead law.
residual_risks: Lake progeny derivation includes capped/audit-needed treatment searches, but the top-level treatment judgment remains good_law.

reasons: Support classification is outside lens B; no treatment or currency defect appears from the disclosed lake record.
The lake treatment scope note treats the vehicle caretaking holding as intact, which is consistent with the page assigning Cady a central community-caretaking role from a currency perspective.
residual_risks: Substantive home-role support was not evaluated under lens B.

residual_risks: Substantive cross-doctrine support was not evaluated under lens B.

reasons: Support classification is outside lens B; no quote or holding-support defect is raised here.
For treatment purposes, the lake scope note says the vehicle caretaking holding is intact and notes only that Caniglia declined to extend the rationale to the home.
residual_risks: Verbatim holding accuracy and quote fidelity remain for lens A.

reasons: Content treatment fields match the lake treatment judgment: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the same vehicle/home scope note.
Lake treatment scope note states that the vehicle caretaking holding is intact and that Caniglia v. Strom declined to extend Cady's caretaking rationale to the home.

All 33 listed treatment edges are marked field_iii mentioned and proposed true; the disclosed record does not contain an actual point override, overruling, supersession, or abrogation of Cady's vehicle holding.
residual_risks: Treatment derivation reports audit_needed and cap_hit for negative/top-cited lanes, so the disclosed record preserves audit risk even though its final judgment is good_law.
Several proposed edges carry negative field_ii labels, but they are not classified as actual negative treatment of Cady in field_iii.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If space permits, state that negative-search candidates in the lake are proposed/mentioned only and no point override is recorded.

reasons: Lake identity identifies the court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus.
The disclosed treatment record marks the federal constitutional vehicle-caretaking holding good_law, so the Binding — SCOTUS weight label is not undermined by the corpus.
residual_risks: The label should not be read to erase the scope limitation that Caniglia declined to extend Cady to homes.
